answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network anchors identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Instead of treating past execution proofs as an inert relic, each node links its verified history across a progressive trust ridge. To deploy multiple identities, Sybil swarms face an umber reserve requirement where capital bonding scales superlinearly: staking cost scales as O(k^2) with cluster size k, imposing exponential capital exhaustion.
